Bromberg brings over 20 years of experience in the online and mobile gaming industry and will advise across Blackstone’s businesses, with a focus on Blackstone Growth (BXG). His expertise is expected to be invaluable to Blackstone's investment teams and portfolio companies, particularly given his background helping companies thrive in the fast-moving gaming sector.

feed.title: Intel Expands Atlanta Presence Across Software Development Team
feed.summary: Intel is significantly expanding its software development team in Atlanta, planning to add over 100 new local jobs with six-figure salaries as part of a larger goal to create 500 jobs by 2024. This move reinforces Atlanta's growing reputation as a tech hub, alongside other major companies like Cash App, Nike, and Microsoft also establishing or expanding their presence in the city. The new roles will focus on areas like AI, cloud, and security, utilizing Atlanta's diverse technology community and talent base.

feed.title: When Momentum Fails
feed.summary: The article discusses how momentum, a historically strong investment factor, has shown signs of faltering in recent months despite its long-term outperformance. It highlights that while momentum stocks have often delivered strong returns, periods of market decline and shifts in investor sentiment can lead to sharp drawdowns, emphasizing that nothing lasts forever in investing.

feed.title: Ten Principles For Designing The Metaverse
feed.summary: This article outlines ten principles for designing the metaverse, emphasizing that while the metaverse doesn't fully exist yet, companies should experiment with virtual 3D worlds. Author David Truog introduces "fusion" and "empiricism" as key principles, explaining how VR, MR, and AR experiences range from physical to entirely mediated, and stressing the importance of direct experience over speculation. The article also touches upon other principles like depth, attention, and magic, all grounded in human-centered design, to help organizations navigate the development of extended reality (XR) experiences.

feed.title: Microsoft Collaborates with Peel District School Board to launch BuildAbility, a new world in Minecraft: Education Edition focused on accessibility and building inclusive spaces - Peel Board Office Site
feed.summary: The Peel District School Board (PDSB) and Microsoft Canada have launched "BuildAbility," a new world in Minecraft: Education Edition designed to teach students about accessibility and inclusive design. This initiative encourages students and educators to identify and eliminate accessibility barriers, promoting empathy for individuals with disabilities. The program aligns with PDSB's multi-year accessibility plan and Ontario's Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, aiming to foster an accessibility-first culture in both online spaces and physical communities.

feed.title: Qualcomm Advances Development of Smarter and Safer Autonomous Robots for Logistics, Industry 4.0, and Urban Aerial Mobility with Next-Generation 5G and AI Robotics Solutions
feed.summary: Qualcomm Technologies has unveiled an expanded roadmap of 5G and edge-AI robotics solutions, including the Qualcomm Robotics RB6 Platform and the Qualcomm RB5 AMR Reference Design. These new solutions aim to enhance autonomy and intelligence for various robotic applications in logistics, manufacturing, and urban air mobility by integrating advanced AI and 5G capabilities. The company is collaborating with multiple industry leaders to foster innovation in this rapidly evolving sector.

feed.title: Walmart hires 1st chief economist
feed.summary: Walmart Inc. has appointed John List, a distinguished professor from the University of Chicago, as its first chief economist. This hiring aims to leverage List's expertise in behavioral economics to better understand customer choices and preferences. The announcement was made by Tom Ward, Walmart U.S. chief e-commerce officer, on LinkedIn.

feed.title: Salesforce To Take Over Troops.ai For Microsoft Teams, Slack Integration Power
feed.summary: Salesforce plans to acquire Troops.ai, a company that provides integration tools for Slack and Microsoft Teams, to enhance its Slack offerings. Troops.ai specializes in delivering real-time insights and revenue signals from CRM systems like Salesforce to communication platforms, aiming to improve sales velocity and collaboration. The acquisition, expected to close before July 31, will integrate Troops.ai's technology into Slack, bolstering its capabilities for customer-facing teams.

feed.title: Rackspace is looking to sell itself and exit the public markets, again
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology Inc. is exploring a sale of all or part of its business to return to private ownership, less than two years after re-entering the public market. The company believes a sum-of-the-parts valuation could exceed its current enterprise value, driven by attractive growth in its public cloud sector. This move follows tepid first-quarter financial results, with a net loss of $64 million and modest revenue growth, prompting concerns about its growth trajectory in comparison to the broader cloud market.

feed.title: Tripolygon, a 3D modeling software developer, lets metaverse creators make their own 3D assets
feed.summary: Tripolygon, a South Korean 3D modeling software developer, offers Unity plugins that allow metaverse creators to easily design their own 3D assets without needing expertise in complex 3D modeling programs. The company recently secured $5.2 million in Series A funding, bringing its total raised to $5.7 million and valuing it at approximately $25 million. Tripolygon aims to democratize 3D asset creation for Unity users, with around 17,000 developers currently using its UModeler product.

feed.title: Intel Introduces Project Amber for Cloud-to-Edge and On-Premises Trust Assurance
feed.summary: Intel announced Project Amber, a new service designed to provide remote verification of trustworthiness in cloud, edge, and on-premises environments, addressing the growing need for enhanced security and confidential computing. The company also detailed its efforts in securing AI deployments through partnerships and outlined a strategy for quantum-resistant cryptography by 2030, beginning with its 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable platform. These initiatives aim to build trust and security for current and future technology landscapes.

feed.title: CISA tells federal agencies to fix actively exploited F5 BIG-IP bug
feed.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has mandated federal agencies to patch a critical F5 BIG-IP vulnerability (CVE-2022-1388) by May 31st, as it is being actively exploited. This bug allows remote attackers to execute commands on unpatched devices, with some threat actors even wiping Linux file systems. While the directive specifically applies to U.S. federal agencies, CISA strongly advises all organizations to fix the flaw immediately.

feed.title: Kraft Heinz thinking outside the ketchup bottle, exploring paper packaging
feed.summary: Kraft Heinz is partnering with UK-based Pulpex to develop paper-based packaging for its condiments, starting with the iconic Heinz Ketchup bottle. This initiative is part of Kraft Heinz's broader commitment to sustainability, including its goal to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. The move reflects the company's efforts to innovate beyond traditional packaging to reduce environmental impact.

feed.title: Rackspace CEO’s comments fuel speculation about another sale of tech company
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology CEO Kevin Jones' recent comments to analysts have sparked speculation about a potential sale or restructuring of the company. Jones indicated that a "sum of the parts valuation" could exceed Rackspace's current enterprise value, leading to considerations of strategic alternatives. While Rackspace later downplayed a full sale, the company is exploring reorganizing its on-premise server and public cloud services into separate entities to "unlock value."

feed.title: Rackspace for sale, looking for privatization
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology, which went public less than two years ago, is seeking privatization due to its market capitalization not reflecting the company's true value. The company, which helps businesses manage cloud environments, needs to make strategic changes to better compete in the growing multicloud market. Although profitable, Rackspace's growth isn't fast enough to satisfy stock market analysts, making privatization an attractive option to allow for necessary repositioning in the market.

feed.title: ScanSource CEO: MSPs Becoming A ‘Source Of Growth’ For The Distributor
feed.summary: ScanSource's top executives discussed their hybrid distribution strategy as a key driver for growth, helping partners connect devices to the cloud. CEO Mike Baur noted that MSPs are a growing part of their business, particularly in the U.K. and Brazil, and are becoming a significant source of growth in the U.S. as ScanSource expands its recurring revenue and SaaS capabilities. The company reported strong financial results for its fiscal third quarter 2022, with total revenue up 15.9 percent.

feed.title: Cohesity protects user data with FortKnox vault service
feed.summary: Cohesity has launched FortKnox, a managed SaaS data protection service that provides an air-gapped digital vault within AWS. This service aims to enhance cyber resilience and recovery times for organizations against ransomware attacks and other disaster recovery concerns. It allows users to create an isolated backup copy of their data, addressing a critical need for robust data protection without requiring extensive in-house expertise.

feed.title: US, allies blame Russia for Viasat cyberattack
feed.summary: The US, UK, and EU authorities have formally attributed a series of cyberattacks preceding Russia's invasion of Ukraine, including a significant attack on Viasat's KA-SAT network, to Russia. The Viasat attack, which utilized AcidRain malware to wipe modems and routers, aimed to disrupt Ukrainian military capabilities but also affected civilian internet users and a European alternative energy provider. This attribution raises questions about potential responses from the US and NATO to such cyberwarfare.

feed.title: Slack and Teams are Replacing Business Emails, Report Shows
feed.summary: A new report indicates that business communication is shifting from traditional email to real-time messaging apps like Slack and Microsoft Teams. This change is driven by a preference for less formal messaging, increased security features like end-to-end encryption, and the rise of hybrid work models. While email still serves for formal communications, chat apps are becoming the preferred method for daily interactions, and businesses are also adopting stronger cybersecurity measures to protect against email-based cyber threats.

feed.title: KKR to buy SK’s gas production facility for more than $785 mn
feed.summary: KKR & Co. is set to acquire SK Materials Airplus Inc.'s industrial gas production facility from SK Inc. for over $785 million, outbidding competitors like Macquarie and Brookfield. The acquisition will secure a steady cash flow for KKR due to SK Materials Airplus's long-term supply contract with SK Hynix. This aligns with KKR's recent active investment strategy in South Korea, particularly in the energy and environmental sectors.
feed.source: The Korea Economic Daily Global Edition
feed.source_domain: The Korea Economic Daily Global Edition

feed.title: Z by HP Powers Today’s Professionals to Create without Limitation
feed.summary: HP announced new Z by HP solutions, including ZBook mobile workstations, Z displays, a Thunderbolt G4 Dock, and tools for data scientists, aimed at empowering creative and technical professionals. These products offer enhanced performance, seamless collaboration, and improved productivity for those working in diverse environments, from on-the-go to hybrid setups. Key features include powerful CPUs/GPUs, high-refresh-rate displays, secure docking, and a new Data Science Stack Manager to streamline workflows.

feed.title: ConnectWise, N-able, Sophos Owner Thoma Bravo Raises $20B+ for Technology Acquisitions
feed.summary: Private equity firm Thoma Bravo, known for owning ConnectWise, N-able, and Sophos, has successfully raised over $20 billion for its new Fund XV despite recent market turbulence. The firm plans to use these funds for further software acquisitions, with CEO Orlando Bravo emphasizing a profit-led approach over "growth at all costs." Thoma Bravo's substantial assets and investment strategy position it as a major player in the cybersecurity and MSP software market, competing with other private equity firms also actively investing in the tech sector.

feed.title: Microsoft Corp. stock falls Thursday, underperforms market
feed.summary: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) stock fell 2.00% on Thursday, closing at $255.35, underperforming the broader market as both the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the second consecutive day of losses for the company, with its stock trading significantly below its 52-week high. Competitors showed mixed performance, with Apple and Alphabet also falling, while SAP SE ADR saw gains.

feed.title: 3 Reasons Advisors Are Adding BLKC & SATO to Portfolios
feed.summary: Advisors are incorporating BLKC and SATO ETFs into portfolios for three main reasons: portfolio diversification, capitalizing on the transformative growth of digital assets, and using them as a potential hedge against inflation. These ETFs offer exposure to the cryptocurrency industry, with BLKC focusing on blockchain developments and SATO on the broader crypto economy. The article highlights the increasing institutional investor interest and the finite supply of some cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin as key attractions.

feed.title: AIIMS Jodhpur collaborates with Microsoft India to establish a Mixed Reality Center of Excellence
feed.summary: AIIMS Jodhpur and Microsoft India are partnering to establish a Mixed Reality Centre of Excellence in Jodhpur. This collaboration aims to transform healthcare services, medical education, and research through digital innovation, including the creation of a Mixed Reality Healthcare Lab and piloting remote healthcare services using devices like HoloLens. This initiative seeks to provide enhanced learning opportunities for medical students and extend healthcare delivery to underserved areas.

feed.title: WD Targets Cloud Challenges
feed.summary: Western Digital (WD) is launching new SSDs and HDDs to address the exponential data growth and performance demands in cloud environments, particularly for hyperscale customers. The company's new 22TB and 26TB UltraSMR HDDs leverage OptiNAND and enhanced SMR technology, while their Ultrastar NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSDs target disaggregated storage in public clouds to improve utilization and density. WD also notes a strong demand for client SSDs driven by remote work and gaming, reinforcing the critical role of storage innovation across the board.

feed.title: Bill Gates Sells $940 Million of CN Rail Stock
feed.summary: Bill Gates' investment firm, Cascade Investment, sold approximately $940 million worth of Canadian National Railway Co. shares between April 27 and May 12, reducing its stake in the company to about 9%. This sale is part of an ongoing reduction in ownership since May 2021. Gates' former wife, Melinda French Gates, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation also sold significant portions of their Canadian National shares.

feed.title: Oracle Corp. stock rises Friday, still underperforms market
feed.summary: Oracle Corp. (ORCL) saw its stock rise 0.62% on Friday to $71.17, despite a generally positive day for the broader market with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also increasing. However, Oracle underperformed compared to some competitors and remained significantly below its 52-week high. Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

feed.title: Cisco PENN1 – Making hybrid work, work for offices
feed.summary: Cisco has transformed its PENN1 office space in New York City into a showcase for hybrid work, utilizing its smart building solutions developed over a decade. By integrating various building systems into a unified network, Cisco has created a collaborative environment designed for flexibility and enhanced user experience. This retrofit, leveraging technologies like Catalyst 9000, Cisco DNA Spaces, and Webex, simplifies management, reduces operational costs, and supports diverse collaboration needs.

feed.title: Trump could be paid to post for his own start-up. (Published 2022)
feed.summary: A new regulatory filing reveals that former President Donald J. Trump could be compensated for posting on his own social media platform, Truth Social, and may not be bound by exclusivity, even allowing him to post on other platforms for political purposes. The filing also warns that regulators might block the merger of Digital World Acquisition Corporation with Trump Media & Technology Group. This arrangement raises concerns about his potential return to Twitter if Elon Musk's acquisition of the platform is completed, despite Trump's stated reluctance.

feed.title: eBay partners with FedEx to ease Canadian shipping
feed.summary: eBay has partnered with FedEx to integrate FedEx shipping services directly into its Canadian online marketplace, eBay Labels. This collaboration aims to provide Canadian sellers with seamless access to domestic and international shipping tools and services at preferential rates, simplifying the shipping process. The partnership also extends FedEx's broader efforts to streamline e-commerce fulfillment for retailers, building on its existing collaboration with Microsoft for "logistics as a service."

feed.title: Microsoft Channel Chief Rodney Clark To Leave After Over A Year In Role
feed.summary: Rodney Clark, Microsoft's channel chief and a 24-year veteran of the company, is departing to take an executive officer role at a publicly traded company that partners with Microsoft. His successor will be announced at the annual Inspire partner conference in July. Microsoft's corporate vice president of global partner solutions, Nick Parker, stated that the company has a strong leadership team in place to ensure continuity for partners and programs.

feed.title: A Look Into Public Clouds From the Ransomware Actor's Perspective
feed.summary: This article examines the potential evolution of ransomware attacks in public cloud environments, proposing that while traditional ransomware is largely ineffective, threat actors could adapt their tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to be cloud-native. It discusses how attackers might gain initial access, execute attacks through control and data plane APIs, and achieve privilege escalation using IAM misconfigurations. The article concludes that public clouds are inherently more resilient to ransomware than on-premises systems, but emphasizes the need for organizations to proactively secure identities and adopt best practices to mitigate theoretical cloud-based ransomware threats.

feed.title: 7 Tips for Conducting Performance Reviews With Remote Employees
feed.summary: This article provides seven tips for conducting effective performance reviews with remote employees, acknowledging the shift to widespread remote work. It covers strategies such as utilizing software for evaluations, conducting calibration sessions with managers, scheduling ample time for discussions, and ensuring a private, distraction-free environment. The guide emphasizes the importance of making remote reviews a permanent, smooth process for organizations adopting remote work by choice.

feed.title: Starbucks to add abortion travel coverage to U.S. health benefits
feed.summary: Starbucks Corp announced it will reimburse U.S. employees for travel expenses if they need to go more than 100 miles from home to obtain an abortion. This decision follows a leaked Supreme Court draft opinion that suggests Roe v. Wade could be overturned, leading to tighter abortion restrictions in some states. Starbucks joins other major companies like Amazon and Microsoft in offering similar benefits.

feed.title: Companies (and government) spending big to produce chips
feed.summary: The Japanese government and companies are investing trillions of yen to revitalize the country's semiconductor industry, aiming to increase domestic production amid a global chip shortage. Through government grants from a 600-billion-yen fund, companies like Kioxia Holdings, TSMC, Sony Group, and Denso are constructing or upgrading factories to produce various types of semiconductors. This initiative seeks to establish a stable domestic supply chain and regain Japan's former prominence in the global semiconductor market, although some experts express concerns about potential interference with free competition due to government support.

feed.title: Starbucks to cover employees’ travel expenses for abortions; gender surgeries
feed.summary: Starbucks announced an expansion of its health care benefits to cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortions or gender-affirming procedures if these services are not available within 100 miles of their homes. This decision comes in the wake of a leaked draft U.S. Supreme Court opinion potentially overturning Roe v. Wade, with the company affirming its commitment to ensuring employee access to quality healthcare. Starbucks joins other major companies in offering this benefit, consistent with its history of advocating for liberal causes.

feed.title: Microchip Adds Real-Time Security to Its Root of Trust Silicon Tech
feed.summary: Microchip has updated its Trust Shield root of trust product with the new CEC1736 controller, adding real-time security features like SPI bus runtime protection to monitor traffic between the CPU and Flash memory. This enhancement aims to prevent firmware attacks, which are increasingly common and often overlooked. The article highlights the growing industry focus on hardware-based root of trust solutions to secure servers and data centers from physical and remote threats, noting similar initiatives from tech giants like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft.

feed.title: Microsoft TechSpark announces expansion to Jackson, Mississippi
feed.summary: Microsoft's TechSpark initiative is expanding to Jackson, Mississippi, to address the digital divide and foster inclusive economic opportunities. The expansion will focus on digital skills training, computer science education, broadband connectivity, and digital transformation for nonprofits and startups, spearheaded by Jackson resident JJ Townsend. Key initial collaborations include supporting Jackson State University's Cybersecurity Readiness program, gener8tor Skills Accelerator, Innovate Mississippi’s CoBuilders Accelerator, and the Jackson Tech District Makerspace.

feed.title: Amazon replaces Microsoft as Seattle area's top corporate giver
feed.summary: Amazon has surpassed Microsoft as the leading corporate philanthropist in the Seattle area, according to a recent report. Amazon significantly increased its charitable giving, particularly in areas like housing, contributing millions more than Microsoft. This shift marks a notable change in the philanthropic landscape of Washington.

feed.title: HP Envy 34 All-in-One Desktop review: A big-screen AIO for power users and creators
feed.summary: HP has updated its Envy All-in-One desktop, featuring a 34-inch 5K wide-screen display, making it a strong alternative to the discontinued 27-inch iMac for creative users and power users. This review highlights its impressive design, versatile features including accessible RAM/SSD slots, and strong performance, especially in graphics, though it notes some bloatware and a lack of display swivel. The Envy 34 offers various configurations, from an entry-level model to a high-end option with a Core i9 processor and RTX 3080 graphics.

feed.title: DevSecOps: Why Security can no longer be an afterthought
feed.summary: This article argues that security can no longer be treated as an afterthought in software development, especially with the shift to cloud environments and the expanding attack surface. It advocates for DevSecOps, a methodology that integrates security into every stage of the development pipeline, emphasizing shared responsibility and secure coding practices. The author highlights the increasing sophistication of cyber threats and the limitations of traditional perimeter security, proposing Zero-Trust as a necessary framework.

feed.title: Why S&P booted Tesla from its ESG index
feed.summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices removed Tesla from its S&P 500 ESG Index due to a decline in its ESG rank compared to global peers. Despite Tesla's role in the transition to electric vehicles, the decision was influenced by claims of racial discrimination, poor working conditions at its factory, and its handling of a federal investigation into autopilot-related deaths. Elon Musk called ESG an "outrageous scam" in response to the decision.

feed.title: With multi-device FIDO credentials, you can now go all-in on passwordless | CXO Revolutionaries
feed.summary: Apple, Google, and Microsoft's expanded support for multi-device FIDO credentials is set to revolutionize passwordless logins, addressing previous limitations of FIDO authentication like device-locked cryptographic keys and complex re-enrollment processes. This development, coupled with the Federal Zero Trust Strategy requiring phishing-resistant authentication, positions FIDO to become a prevalent, high-assurance authentication method for both consumers and federal use cases. The update promises seamless and secure access to FIDO credentials across multiple devices, even after device replacement.

feed.title: Clorox Announces Appointment of Julia Denman and Stephanie Plaines to its Board of Directors
feed.summary: The Clorox Company announced the appointment of Julia Denman and Stephanie Plaines to its board of directors, expanding the board to 13 members. Both Denman and Plaines bring extensive financial expertise and leadership experience from various sectors, enriching the board's diversity and qualifications. They are expected to serve on the audit committee, contributing to Clorox's strategic goals and stakeholder value.

feed.title: Citrix Systems Inc. stock outperforms market despite losses on the day
feed.summary: Shares of Citrix Systems Inc. slipped on Wednesday, but still outperformed major market indices and some competitors. The stock closed below its 52-week high, and trading volume was lower than its 50-day average.

feed.title: Microsoft moves forward with massive corporate campus project in Atlanta
feed.summary: Microsoft is proceeding with ambitious plans to develop a massive 90-acre corporate campus in Atlanta, Georgia, over the next decade, expecting to create thousands of jobs. The project, located at Quarry Yards, will dedicate 25% of the property to community projects like affordable housing and grocery stores, and Microsoft is actively seeking community feedback for the site's design with a strong focus on sustainability. Local politicians and community leaders have expressed enthusiasm for the economic and social benefits the campus will bring to Atlanta.

feed.title: Kitchen Brains Accelerates Growth with Investment from Source Capital
feed.summary: Kitchen Brains, a designer and manufacturer of smart cooking computers and software solutions for commercial foodservice, has been acquired by Source Capital, LLC. The investment aims to accelerate Kitchen Brains' product pipeline, bolster scalability, and provide greater access to financial and human capital resources. Kitchen Brains plans to deepen existing customer relationships and expand its hardware and software offerings globally.

feed.title: Mobile Gaming Market Size to grow by USD 66.43 billion | 47% of the growth will originate from APAC| Technavio
feed.summary: The mobile gaming market is projected to grow by USD 66.43 billion at a CAGR of 12.26% between 2021 and 2026, with 47% of this growth coming from the APAC region. The market's expansion is driven by the increasing popularity of multiplayer mobile games and the development of advanced smartphones, encouraging online platform growth. However, the rise of alternative gaming platforms like consoles poses a challenge to market growth.

feed.title: American Makes Microsoft Azure Preferred Cloud Provider for Airline Applications
feed.summary: American Airlines has chosen Microsoft Azure as its preferred cloud platform for various airline applications, including airport taxiing decisions and managing operational data. This move follows previous partnerships with IBM, and American Airlines aims to leverage Azure's AI, machine learning, and data analytics to optimize customer experience and operations, particularly for gating decisions at its DFW hub. This decision positions American Airlines among other major U.S. carriers embracing cloud-first approaches for future resilience and innovation.

feed.title: Xendit Raises US$300M Series D Funding Co-Led by Coatue and Insight Partners Powering Payments for Startups and SMEs in Fastest-Growing Digital Economy
feed.summary: Xendit, a rapidly growing payments infrastructure platform in Southeast Asia, has secured US$300 million in Series D funding, co-led by Coatue and Insight Partners. This new injection of capital brings their total raised to US$538 million, intended to further expand their services and market reach in the region's burgeoning digital economy. The company has demonstrated significant growth, tripling annualized transactions and increasing total payments value, solidifying its position as a key player for startups and SMEs in Southeast Asia.

feed.title: A systems analyst in the age of digital transformation
feed.summary: This article highlights the critical role of a business systems analyst, like Regina Mary Saurimuthu at Flex, in integrating advanced manufacturing technologies with company strategy during the Age of Digital Transformation. It showcases how digitalization and automation are transforming processes at Flex, eliminating manual tasks, and improving efficiency. The piece also touches upon Regina's personal journey, demonstrating resilience and the supportive culture at Flex, while expressing excitement for future technological advancements in manufacturing.

feed.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise announces new supercomputer factory in Europe
feed.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is establishing a new factory in Kutná Hora, Czech Republic, dedicated to manufacturing high-performance computing (HPC) and AI systems. This facility, set to open in summer 2022, will produce HPE Apollo systems and HPC Cray EX supercomputers, with features designed for liquid cooling and heavy equipment. The initiative underscores HPE's commitment to supporting European scientific research and digital sovereignty, partnering with Foxconn for manufacturing and contributing to projects like the EuroHPC JU and LUMI supercomputer.

feed.title: Nevada regulators grant investor Barry Diller limited license as MGM board member
feed.summary: The Nevada Gaming Commission granted media mogul Barry Diller a two-year limited gaming license to serve on the MGM Resorts International board due to an ongoing federal investigation into his stock purchases. Regulators cited Diller's cooperation with the SEC regarding Activision Blizzard Inc. stock acquired before Microsoft's announced acquisition, which resulted in a $60 million profit for him and associates. Despite MGM's legal team arguing for a full license, and Diller denying any wrongdoing, commissioners opted for a limited license to allow time for the federal inquiry to conclude.

feed.title: Report: EA Almost Merged With NBC Universal Before Deal With Comcast Dissolved
feed.summary: A report indicates that Electronic Arts (EA) was close to merging with NBC Universal, with talks dissolving in April over monetary and corporate structure disagreements. Comcast's chairman and CEO, Brian Roberts, reportedly sought to bring EA under NBCUniversal's umbrella for new IP. Despite this failed deal, EA is also reportedly exploring a "more meaningful relationship" with Disney, potentially uniting ESPN and EA Sports.

feed.title: From Bitcoin to the Metaverse: The current evolution is a revolution
feed.summary: This article discusses the evolution of cryptocurrency from Bitcoin to the Metaverse, highlighting key technological advancements and the increasing cybersecurity threats in the Web3 space. Check Point Research details how vulnerabilities in leading platforms have led to billions in losses and emphasizes the critical need for enhanced security measures and expert involvement in this rapidly expanding digital frontier.

feed.title: The best places to work in 2022, ranked
feed.summary: Glassdoor has released its list of the best companies to work for in 2022, based on over 100 million employee reviews covering nine workplace attributes. While tech companies dominate the top spots due to flexible environments and good benefits, the list also includes companies from diverse industries such as healthcare, retail, and finance. NVIDIA, HubSpot, and Box are highlighted as some of the top-ranked companies.

feed.title: Tech Industry Vet Brian Roach to Join Red River as CEO
feed.summary: Brian Roach, a veteran of the technology industry, has been appointed as the new CEO of Red River, effective May 31. He previously led SAP's North American regulated industries practice and has held leadership roles at Juniper Networks, Microsoft, Lockheed Martin, and Unisys. Red River, a portfolio company of Cerberus Capital Management, specializes in IT support services including cloud, security, and networking.

feed.title: NBC Universal acquisition of Electronic Arts fell apart at the last second
feed.summary: A proposed merger between Comcast/NBC Universal and Electronic Arts fell through due to disagreements over price and structure. The deal would have seen NBCUniversal spun off and combined with EA, with EA's CEO Andrew Wilson potentially leading the new entity. This acquisition was considered in the wake of other major gaming industry mergers, highlighting the ongoing consolidation trend.

feed.title: International Business Machines Corp. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
feed.summary: International Business Machines Corp. (IBM) stock fell 0.91% to $128.48 on Friday, May 20, 2022, underperforming the broader stock market, which saw the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average rise slightly. This marked the third consecutive day of losses for IBM, leaving its stock $17.51 below its 52-week high. While IBM declined, some competitors showed mixed performance, with Apple Inc. (AAPL) rising and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) and Alphabet Inc. Cl A (GOOGL) falling.

feed.title: WacoWatch
feed.summary: Judge Albright granted Microsoft Corporation's motion to transfer a patent litigation case to the Western District of Washington, finding it to be a more convenient venue. The decision was based on an analysis of private and public interest factors, including the location of evidence and witnesses, and despite the plaintiff's argument about Microsoft's past venue practices. Three factors favored transfer, one disfavored it, and four were neutral.

feed.title: Digital Marketing Software Market Giants Spending Is Going to Boom | Major Giants IBM, HubSpot, Microsoft
feed.summary: A new study by HTF MI reveals that the worldwide digital marketing software market is expected to boom, with major players like IBM, HubSpot, and Microsoft driving growth. The research provides an in-depth analysis of market trends, drivers, and future prospects, covering segmentation by application (Large Enterprises & SMEs) and product type (On-Premises & Cloud). The report also highlights key market developments and includes a geographical analysis of the market.

feed.title: First Corsair gaming laptop is AMD-powered and has a touch bar
feed.summary: Corsair is entering the gaming laptop market with its new Voyager a1600 AMD Advantage Edition, exclusively featuring AMD Ryzen 6000-series CPUs and Radeon RX 6000 series GPUs. A distinctive feature is its LCD touch bar with customizable S-key shortcut buttons, accessible even when the laptop is closed, and powered by Elgato Stream Deck software, targeting mobile streamers. The laptop boasts a 240Hz 16-inch display, DDR5 RAM, and an advanced vapor chamber cooling system.

feed.title: Trump sues Facebook, Twitter, Google for ‘censorship’, launches his own social media platform
feed.summary: Former President Donald Trump filed class-action lawsuits against Facebook, Twitter, and Google for alleged "censorship" after his accounts were restricted or suspended following the Jan. 6, 2021 Capitol attack. The lawsuits claim these platforms, by coordinating with government entities, act as "state actors" and thus violate his First Amendment rights, though legal experts and court rulings have largely dismissed these arguments. Concurrently, Trump launched his own social media platform, "Truth Social," designed to be a "Big Tent" alternative to mainstream platforms.

feed.title: Take-Two completes $12.7B acquisition of mobile games giant Zynga
feed.summary: Take-Two has completed its $12.7 billion acquisition of mobile games giant Zynga, bringing popular titles like Farmville and Words With Friends under its ownership. This strategic move aims to significantly increase Take-Two's net bookings from the fast-growing mobile gaming segment and enable substantial cost synergies and revenue opportunities. The acquisition merges two gaming powerhouses, expanding Take-Two's mobile presence and providing Zynga access to a vast library of franchises for new gaming experiences.

feed.title: U.S. company building AI supercomputer factory in Central Bohemia
feed.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise is establishing its first European factory for next-generation high-performance computing and AI systems in Kutná Hora, Central Bohemia, Czech Republic. This new facility will manufacture custom-designed supercomputers primarily for scientific research, expanding HPE's global manufacturing footprint. The factory will focus on producing liquid-cooled HPC and AI systems, including HPE Apollo and HPE Cray EX supercomputers, with operations set to begin in summer 2022.

feed.title: Companies perform better if they’re more inclusive: Take these 3 steps to increase diversity
feed.summary: This article argues that diversity and inclusion are crucial for a company's innovation, profitability, and overall success. It highlights research by Gartner and McKinsey & Company showing improved team performance and higher profitability in diverse environments. The author provides three actionable steps for organizations to increase diversity: actively recruiting diverse candidates, creating channels for honest feedback, and continuously discussing inclusivity.

feed.title: Interxion pauses plans for $300 million expansion in Dublin
feed.summary: Interxion has paused a $300 million expansion plan in Dublin due to a de facto moratorium placed on new data center developments in the greater Dublin area by EirGrid, Ireland's national grid operator. This moratorium, which could last until 2028, has led to calls for a nationwide ban and has prompted criticism from various industry bodies, despite local council efforts to prevent further data center construction. The situation highlights the growing pressure on Ireland's energy resources from data centers, which now consume 11 percent of the country's total grid-generated electricity.

feed.title: Microsoft Technology Center in Zurich officially opened
feed.summary: Microsoft Switzerland has officially opened its Microsoft Technology Center (MTC) at its new headquarters in The Circle at the Zurich Airport. This 1,000 square meter space is designed to be an innovation hub where customers can envision and test new technology and industry-specific scenarios. The MTC represents a significant investment by Microsoft to drive innovation and co-innovation in Switzerland, built on over 30 years of local presence and partnerships.

feed.title: Exclusive: Oracle to win unconditional EU nod for $28.3 billion Cerner deal
feed.summary: Oracle is expected to receive unconditional EU antitrust clearance for its $28.3 billion acquisition of U.S. healthcare IT company Cerner Corp. This deal, Oracle's largest ever, aims to boost its cloud platform by leveraging Cerner's data for AI-based cloud services and attracting more healthcare clients. The European Commission is scheduled to decide on the deal by June 1.

feed.title: Beware emailed PDFs containing Word docs exploiting old bugs
feed.summary: HP cybersecurity researchers have discovered an email campaign distributing malware through PDFs that embed malicious Word documents, exploiting a four-year-old Microsoft Office vulnerability (CVE-2017-11882). This unusual method leverages user trust in PDF documents to deliver the Snake Keylogger, highlighting that old vulnerabilities remain effective and emphasizing the need for patching, user education, and robust email security.

feed.title: How Amazon, Microsoft, Costco and more Seattle-area brands rank by reputation
feed.summary: Amazon ranked highest among Seattle-area companies in a recent Axios and Harris Poll survey assessing the reputations of the 100 most visible corporate brands in the U.S. Conversely, Costco, based in Issaquah, experienced a 17-place drop in the same survey. The article highlights how local companies performed in this national reputational ranking.

feed.title: Apple's Steve Jobs: An Extraordinary Career
feed.summary: This article chronicles the extraordinary career of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, highlighting how his vision propelled the PC revolution and Apple's success. It covers his early life, his initial departure from Apple, his ventures with NeXT and Pixar, and his triumphant return to Apple, where he spearheaded groundbreaking products like the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad. The piece concludes with his health struggles, resignation, and passing, emphasizing his lasting legacy as a visionary leader.

feed.title: ServiceNow procurement software centralizes teams, processes
feed.summary: ServiceNow has introduced new procurement management software as part of its Now Platform's San Diego release, aiming to centralize procurement teams and processes, automate workflows, and improve visibility. This offering, called Procurement Service Management, is designed to simplify source-to-pay processes, limit irregular procurement actions, and allow teams to focus on more strategic tasks by automating repetitive operations. It is compatible with existing ERP systems like SAP Ariba and Coupa Procurement through ServiceNow's Integration Hub technology.

feed.title: Qualcomm CEO sees growth in high-end phones even if economy slows
feed.summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon believes the company will continue to see growth in the high-end smartphone market, despite concerns about an economic slowdown. He noted that consumers are increasingly seeking "better phones" with more capabilities, and Qualcomm is gaining market share in premium devices. Amon also highlighted the potential for augmented reality to become as significant as smartphones, expanding Qualcomm's partnerships in the AR/VR space.

feed.title: L’OFFICIEL Makes Its Arrival in the Metaverse with Virtual Land on The Sandbox
feed.summary: Fashion magazine L’OFFICIEL has launched its presence in the metaverse with virtual land on The Sandbox, inspired by sci-fi films like Dune and Total Recall. This "L’OFFICIEL Land" is designed as an open-air exhibition and digital theatre to showcase the magazine's 100-year content history and future editorial focused on Web3 fashion. The initiative, led by Benjamin Eymère, CEO of L’OFFICIEL and Chief Metaverse Officer of AMTD group, marks a significant move into immersive digital experiences for the brand.

feed.title: Broadcom to Buy VMware for $61 Billion in Record Chip Deal
feed.summary: Broadcom Inc. has agreed to acquire cloud-computing company VMware Inc. for approximately $61 billion, marking one of the largest technology deals in history. This acquisition will strengthen Broadcom's software portfolio, a key part of CEO Hock Tan's strategy to diversify the chipmaker and expand its presence in corporate software. The deal, supported by major VMware shareholders, includes commitments for $32 billion in debt financing and is expected to close in Broadcom’s fiscal year 2023.

feed.title: How to Connect With German Software Buyers
feed.summary: This article provides insights into the behavior and preferences of German software buyers, highlighting the country's significant and growing software market. It emphasizes the importance of understanding challenges, valuing detailed specifications, demonstrating compatibility, and providing localized content and support to successfully engage and convert German B2B customers. The piece also stresses the need for a strong onboarding process and ongoing customer engagement to retain clients in this competitive market.

feed.title: Broadcom buys VMware in a $61B acquisition deal
feed.summary: Broadcom has formally announced plans to acquire VMware in a cash and stock deal valued at approximately $61 billion, plus an additional $8 billion in VMware net debt. The deal is expected to close in Broadcom's 2023 financial year, pending regulatory and shareholder approvals. This acquisition will see Broadcom's existing infrastructure and security software integrated into an expanded VMware portfolio, with the Broadcom Software Group rebranding to operate as VMware.

feed.title: Cisco Takes Top Spot In Gartner Supply Chain Top 25 Despite Record Backlog
feed.summary: Cisco maintained its leading position in Gartner's Global Supply Chain Top 25 report for the third consecutive year, despite facing record-breaking customer order backlogs due to ongoing supply chain challenges. The tech giant's proactive strategies, including investing $10 billion to secure chip supplies, adapting its operations, and focusing on ESG and circular economy concepts, contributed to its continued success. Cisco is also mitigating disruptions by working closely with suppliers, optimizing logistics, and promoting refurbished equipment through its Cisco Refresh program.

feed.title: Johnson Controls Appoints Rodney Clark as Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer
feed.summary: Johnson Controls (NYSE: JCI) has appointed Rodney Clark as vice president and chief commercial officer, effective June 1, 2022. Clark will be responsible for leading the company's global sales excellence and growth strategy, particularly focusing on decarbonization in smart, healthy buildings. He joins Johnson Controls from Microsoft, where he previously held significant roles in global partner sales and Internet of Things (IoT) sales.

feed.title: Ampere Roadmap Has Four Future Arm Server Chips
feed.summary: Ampere Computing has outlined its future Arm server chip roadmap, revealing plans for three new processors beyond the recently announced AmpereOne ("Siryn") chip, extending through 2025. The company emphasizes its agile development approach and customer-driven roadmap, focusing on a continuous cadence of releases rather than yearly changes, with hyperscalers influencing chip features and lifespan. The roadmap details expected advancements in core count, process technology (moving to 5nm and 3nm), memory (DDR5, DDR6), and PCI-Express versions for these upcoming chips, while also hinting at a future shift to chiplet architectures.

feed.title: Broadcom to buy Palo Alto’s VMware for $61 billion
feed.summary: Computer chip and software maker Broadcom is set to acquire Palo Alto-based cloud technology company VMware for approximately $61 billion, including $8 billion of VMware's net debt. This acquisition aims to strengthen Broadcom's position in the cloud computing market by integrating VMware's technology. The deal is one of the largest this year, highlighting a trend of significant tech buyouts amidst market uncertainty where tech companies are perceived to be undervalued.

feed.title: Broadcom will tame the VMware beast
feed.summary: Broadcom's planned acquisition of VMware for $61 billion signifies a new era for the virtualization leader, focusing on financial performance and shareholder value. The article details Broadcom's strategy of optimizing profitability by focusing on recurring revenue, cutting R&D and sales/marketing expenses for less profitable areas, and standardizing G&A. For customers, this likely means higher prices and a more focused product portfolio, with core offerings like vSphere being emphasized while less profitable or unproven ventures like Project Monterey face scrutiny.

feed.title: What Is Web 3.0, and How Does It Impact Digital Marketers?
feed.summary: Web 3.0 represents the next stage of internet evolution, offering enhanced data privacy, security, and a more personalized user experience through decentralization and blockchain technology. This shift will significantly impact digital marketers by changing data collection methods, improving user experience, and necessitating updates to current marketing strategies to leverage new data sources and address the move away from third-party cookies. B2B software marketers are advised to stay informed on trends, understand blockchain, and utilize customer data insights to prepare for this new era.

feed.title: The Hanover Insurance Group’s automation CoE ensures successful solutions can scale
feed.summary: The Hanover Insurance Group established an automation Center of Excellence (CoE) to drive digital transformation and improve productivity. By leveraging Microsoft Power Platform, particularly Microsoft Power Automate, the company has successfully scaled solutions across various departments, enhancing business decision-making, stakeholder relationships, and employee efficiency. The CoE aims to integrate automation into daily operations, demonstrating its success through use cases like the FastTrack renewal prep solution and a Surety Commission automation that prevented significant business disruption.

feed.title: Global Data Annotation Tools Market Size, Share Forecast to 2033
feed.summary: The global data annotation tools market was valued at USD 2.87 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 23.82 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 26.50%. Key growth drivers include the rapid penetration of AI in healthcare and massive data generation via advanced technologies, while the inaccuracy of some tools remains a restraint. Asia Pacific is expected to dominate the market, with North America also showing significant growth.

feed.title: Keeping up with manufacturing innovation
feed.summary: Paul Baldassari, President of Manufacturing and Services at Flex, discusses how manufacturers are adapting to constant change, particularly focusing on the rapid digital transformation spurred by the pandemic and supply chain disruptions. He highlights the importance of digitization, automation, AI, and big data analytics for operational efficiency and innovation. The article also emphasizes the shift towards faster, smaller, and more regionalized manufacturing, supported by robotics, automation, and continuous upskilling of the workforce.

feed.title: Threat Brief: CVE-2022-30190 – MSDT Code Execution Vulnerability
feed.summary: Palo Alto Networks has released a threat brief regarding CVE-2022-30190, also known as Follina, a critical Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) remote code execution vulnerability. This exploit allows attackers to bypass Office macro policies and execute code with the same privileges as the calling application, even potentially through zero-click methods. Palo Alto Networks details the attack mechanism, which leverages malicious Word documents with remote templates to execute PowerShell commands, and provides guidance for customers to implement protections using their product suite until Microsoft releases a patch.

feed.title: Michal Braverman-Blumenstyk appointed as CTO for Microsoft’s new Security, Compliance
feed.summary: Microsoft has appointed Michal Braverman-Blumenstyk as Chief Technology Officer for its new Security, Compliance, Identity, and Management Division. She will continue to serve as General Manager of Microsoft Israel R&D Center and her appointment is part of a comprehensive company-wide reorganization merging all security products into a single division. Braverman-Blumenstyk has a strong background in cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, having founded the Microsoft Cyber Security Center in Israel and significantly grown the Israel R&D Center's workforce.

feed.title: Apple Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
feed.summary: Apple Inc.'s stock (AAPL) fell 0.53% to $148.84 on Tuesday, underperforming the broader market as the NASDAQ Composite Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. This marked the end of a three-day winning streak for Apple, and the stock closed $34.10 below its 52-week high. Competitors showed mixed results, with Microsoft (MSFT) and IBM (IBM) also falling, while Alphabet (GOOGL) saw a gain.

feed.title: Hackers ransom 1,200 exposed Elasticsearch databases
feed.summary: Threat actors have hijacked over 1,200 unsecured Elasticsearch databases, replacing data with ransom demands for bitcoin payments. The attackers leveraged automated scripts to find instances with open read/write operations, not exploiting vulnerabilities, but rather misconfigurations. Secureworks reports that while ransom demands totaled over $280,000, there's no indication any payments were made or that data was backed up, making restoration unlikely.

feed.title: Bill Gates on the Next 40 Years in Technology
feed.summary: In an interview with PCMag, Bill Gates reflects on the past 40 years of technology since the original IBM PC and offers insights into the future. He discusses the ubiquitous nature of the personal computer, the challenges of climate change and political polarization, and the potential of AI and biological advances. Gates also shares his current technology usage and how it compares to early computing, highlighting the immense progress made.

feed.title: Read the Charter Issue of PC Magazine From 1982
feed.summary: This article looks back at the origin of PC Magazine, which started in 1982 alongside the introduction of the IBM PC. It details the challenges, successes, and key figures, like founder David Bunnell, involved in launching the publication. The piece also highlights how PC Magazine adapted through the years, from print to digital, while enduring rivalries and major industry shifts.

feed.title: La fórmula tecnológica que lleva a Cemex a la nube
feed.summary: Cemex has embarked on a three-stage digital transformation journey, primarily focusing on migrating its IT architecture to the cloud with Microsoft Azure. This initiative aims to improve customer experience, synchronize services across its global operations, and increase efficiency and performance, particularly by moving critical SAP systems to Azure and SUSE Linux Enterprise Server. The company achieved significant performance improvements and cost reductions through this migration.

feed.title: Diablo Immortal Review
feed.summary: This extensive review of Diablo Immortal dives into Blizzard's free-to-play mobile MMO action-RPG, highlighting its core Diablo elements despite its mobile platform and microtransaction systems. The author praises its depth, storyline, and optimization, while noting it might not be welcoming for new Diablo players. Despite initial skepticism about mobile games and monetization, the review concludes that Diablo Immortal is shaping up to be one of the best mobile offerings available.

feed.title: Short-term profits and long-term consequences — did Jack Welch break capitalism?
feed.summary: This article examines the legacy of Jack Welch, former CEO of General Electric, through an interview with New York Times correspondent David Gelles. Gelles argues in his book "The Man Who Broke Capitalism" that Welch's ruthless cost-cutting, focus on short-term profits, and practices like "stack ranking" ultimately harmed GE, American workers, and capitalism itself. The interview discusses GE's historical significance, Welch's management style, the impact of his policies on employees, and the eventual dismantling of GE into three separate companies.

feed.title: MyDIGITAL and Microsoft commit to innovation, digital skills, and building economic resilience for Malaysia
feed.summary: MyDIGITAL and Microsoft announced the MyDIGITAL GovTech Innovation partnership in Malaysia, focusing on enhancing digital skills for civil servants and strengthening the nation's economic resilience. This initiative builds on existing collaborations, aiming for widespread cloud adoption and digital literacy within the government by 2025. Microsoft reaffirms its commitment to Malaysia's digital transformation, celebrating 30 years in the country with goals to skill 300,000 people by 2024 and an additional 1 million Malaysians by the end of 2023.

feed.title: Cloud stocks mount big rally led by UiPath, as investors bet tech valuations have bottomed
feed.summary: Cloud stocks experienced a significant rally on Thursday, led by UiPath, as investors sought to buy discounted shares of companies heavily impacted by recent market sell-offs. Despite the strong gains, many of these stocks, including UiPath, remain down substantially for the year. The rally occurred even as Microsoft announced trimmed quarterly guidance, indicating that investors might be betting on a bottom for tech valuations.

feed.title: Microsoft adopts principles for employee organizing and engagement with labor organizations
feed.summary: Microsoft has announced new principles for employee organizing and engagement with labor organizations, acknowledging the evolving nature of the American economy and changing expectations about work. The company recognizes employees' legal right to form or join a union and commits to collaborative approaches with unions while maintaining close relationships with all employees. This proactively addresses unionization campaigns, including those in the tech sector, by establishing a framework for dialogue and cooperation.

feed.title: Microsoft introduces Microsoft Entra to help customers secure access in a connected world
feed.summary: Microsoft has launched a new product family called Microsoft Entra, which consolidates all of its identity and access capabilities. This includes Azure Active Directory, a new Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM) solution called Microsoft Entra Permissions Management, and a decentralized identity offering, Microsoft Entra Verified ID. The initiative aims to provide a unified trust fabric for the digital ecosystem, securing access across various cloud environments and enabling privacy-respecting digital interactions.

feed.title: Accenture, Microsoft and Avanade expand partnership to help organizations tackle their greatest sustainability challenges
feed.summary: Accenture, Microsoft, and Avanade have expanded their partnership to help organizations address sustainability challenges, with an initial focus on achieving net zero and future plans for broader ESG issues. They will invest in co-developing carbon-efficient solutions and offer advisory services for reducing emissions, transitioning to new energy sources, and minimizing waste. The collaboration will target digital manufacturing transitions, low carbon energy transitions, sustainable IT with Microsoft Azure, and ESG measurement and analytics using the Microsoft Cloud for Sustainability.

feed.title: ASGN Acquires ServiceNow IT Consulting Partner GlideFast for $350M -
feed.summary: ASGN is acquiring GlideFast Consulting, a ServiceNow IT consulting partner, for $350 million in cash from private equity firm BV Investment Partners. The deal is expected to close in July 2022 and aligns with ASGN's strategic growth plan to reach $6 billion in revenues by 2024. GlideFast, founded in 2015, expects to generate $95 million in revenue for 2022 with mid-teen EBITDA margins.

feed.title: A digital conflict between Russia and Ukraine rages on behind the scenes of war
feed.summary: A behind-the-scenes digital conflict is ongoing between Russia and Ukraine, with the U.S. also conducting offensive cyber operations. Microsoft's Head of Customer Security and Trust, Tom Burt, details how the company has observed destructive cyberattacks leading up to and during the invasion, noting similarities between Russian cyber and physical military objectives. This "hybrid war" poses a threat of collateral damage to Western companies, highlighting the critical role of private sector insights and collaboration with governments.

feed.title: What Can a Multi-Factor Screening Methodology Do for Your Core Equity Exposure?
feed.summary: This article discusses how applying a multi-factor screening methodology, focusing on value, quality, and momentum, can enhance core equity exposure for large-cap stock portfolios. It highlights research from FlexShares suggesting that this approach can deliver superior risk-adjusted returns compared to the broad large-cap market. The FlexShares US Quality Large Cap Index Fund (QLC) is presented as an example of an ETF that utilizes these factors.

feed.title: Investing in Big Data with Data Center REITs
feed.summary: This article explores the concept of investing in data center Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) as a way to gain exposure to the big data sector. While acknowledging the appeal of REITs for diversification and income, the authors argue that data center REITs carry significant risks, resembling tech stocks more than traditional real estate investments. They conclude that such REITs offer too much risk without sufficient upside potential, suggesting alternative investments like NVIDIA for data center growth exposure.

feed.title: What Can a Multi-Factor Screening Methodology Do for Your Core Equity Exposure?
feed.summary: This article discusses how applying a multi-factor screening methodology can improve risk-adjusted returns for large-cap equity portfolios. It highlights factors such as value, quality, and momentum, and introduces the FlexShares US Quality Large Cap Index Fund (QLC) which integrates these factors. The fund aims to provide benefits of these factor exposures while maintaining a similar risk profile to the broader large-cap market.

feed.title: Teresa Carlson returns to Microsoft
feed.summary: Teresa Carlson has rejoined Microsoft as a corporate Vice President and executive-in-residence, nearly 12 years after her previous departure. Carlson, a prominent figure in government cloud computing, left Amazon Web Services where she led their public sector growth, and then had a brief stint as chief growth officer at Splunk before her recent move back to Microsoft. Her return marks a significant development in her career trajectory within the technology industry.

feed.title: MicroStrategy Incorporated Class A (MSTR)
feed.summary: This page provides a detailed stock card for MicroStrategy Incorporated Class A (MSTR), showing its current share price, market capitalization, key financial ratios, and historical performance. It also includes peer comparisons, shareholding patterns, and an overview of the company's business as a bitcoin treasury and AI-powered enterprise analytics software provider. The article details FAQs related to the stock's price, ratios, 52-week range, and market cap.

feed.title: Nvidia TAO Toolkit update aims to simplify deep learning model development
feed.summary: Nvidia has updated its TAO Toolkit platform to simplify and accelerate deep learning model creation for enterprise applications, making AI development more accessible and less time-consuming. The toolkit now includes new capabilities like "bring your own model weights" and integration with TensorBoard for better visualization, along with the option to deploy as-a-service with REST APIs. While other companies have also worked on simplifying AI pipelines, analysts note that Nvidia's TAO Toolkit, with its low-code nature and pre-trained models, aims to speed up time-to-market for AI models and reduce the need for extensive data science expertise.

feed.title: New report points to cyber risks in TVA control systems
feed.summary: A recent oversight report revealed that the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) failed to properly implement cybersecurity standards for a control system managing flood and river systems in seven southeastern states. The report identified "inappropriate logical and physical access" and vulnerable operating systems at dams within the system. While the risk of a physical threat was considered low, the lack of clear ownership for the system's maintenance and operation heightened cybersecurity risks, prompting TVA to agree with the findings and commit to updates and clearer responsibilities.

feed.title: Gen-trepreneur Z is making its mark on the future of small business
feed.summary: A Microsoft Store report "Small Business State of Mind" highlights how Generation Z is redefining entrepreneurship. Gen Z small business owners prioritize social good, work unconventional hours, and are using platforms like TikTok for business advice, aiming for early retirement rather than traditional corporate paths. The article emphasizes their unique perspective on work, success, and the future of small business, despite challenges like inflation and data security risks.

feed.title: 7 Blue-Chip Stocks to Buy for June 2022
feed.summary: This article identifies seven blue-chip stocks for investors to consider buying in June 2022, emphasizing their stability and long-term potential amidst economic uncertainty. The list includes McDonald’s, Danaher, AT&T, Lockheed Martin, Microsoft, Chevron, and United Parcel Service, highlighting each company's resilience, strong fundamentals, and potential benefits like dividends or defensive qualities. The author suggests these large-cap companies offer a solid foundation for a portfolio, especially during turbulent economic times.

feed.title: DocuSign and Microsoft Deepen Relationship to Accelerate Anywhere Work
feed.summary: DocuSign and Microsoft have expanded their global strategic partnership to enhance how people collaborate and reach agreements digitally, particularly in the "anywhere economy." This collaboration involves new integrations and features across Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform, aiming to streamline agreement processes, increase efficiency, and support remote work. Both companies will also deepen their use of each other's products to further automate internal workflows.

feed.title: Why Has Microsoft Stock Been Falling; Will It Rebound? (NASDAQ:MSFT)
feed.summary: Microsoft's stock has fallen 25% since its November peak, influenced by macroeconomic headwinds and a recent lowering of its fiscal fourth-quarter EPS and revenue guidance due to foreign exchange rates. Bears highlight these challenges, while bulls focus on the company's cloud business and other growth initiatives as potential rebound drivers. The article, written by Chuck Walston, explores these contrasting views on MSFT's future performance.

feed.title: Intel Demonstrates Commitment to Security at RSA Conference 2022
feed.summary: At RSA Conference 2022, Intel reinforced its commitment to security, showcasing innovations and partnerships aimed at addressing complex cyber challenges like hybrid workforces and connected devices. The company highlighted new solutions such as the Intel® NetSec Accelerator Reference Design, the expansion of Project Circuit Breaker, and advancements in hardware-based security with the Intel vPro® platform and confidential computing initiatives like Project Amber. Intel emphasized its holistic approach to security, spanning products, research, and ecosystem collaboration.

feed.title: Oracle quietly closes $28B deal to buy electronic health records company Cerner
feed.summary: Oracle has officially closed its $28 billion acquisition of electronic health records company Cerner, a deal initially announced just before Christmas last year. This move positions Oracle deeper into the healthcare market, aiming to bring Cerner's extensive workload to the Oracle cloud. Analyst Holger Mueller highlighted the strategic importance of this acquisition for Oracle's presence in a rapidly growing vertical industry.

feed.title: Oracle closes $28B deal to buy EHR giant Cerner
feed.summary: Oracle has finalized its $28.3 billion acquisition of health IT company Cerner, marking its largest acquisition to date and a significant move to expand into the healthcare market. The deal, which involved Oracle finalizing a stock tender offer with 69.2% of Cerner shares, aims to leverage Cerner as an "anchor asset" to scale Oracle's cloud business in hospitals and health systems. This acquisition positions Oracle to transform healthcare delivery through new information systems and addresses the growing trend of big tech companies investing heavily in the healthcare IT sector.

feed.title: Weisong Shi recognized as leader in electric vehicle revolution
feed.summary: Weisong Shi, a professor at Wayne State’s College of Engineering and leader of the Wayne Mobility Initiative, has been recognized by Crain’s Detroit Business as a notable leader in electric vehicles. His work in edge computing has influenced various industries, and he is the only academic on the prestigious list. Shi discusses the evolving mobility industry, the role of sensors, Wayne State's contributions to electric vehicle education, and how engineering training has adapted to new technologies.

feed.title: InfoComm Panel: Enter The Metaverse, What Virtual Worlds Mean For AV
feed.summary: An InfoComm panel discussed the metaverse's impact on audiovisual and design professionals, emphasizing its role as a new channel for marketing, training, entertainment, and work. Panelists urged businesses to strategically incorporate the metaverse, starting small and aligning initiatives with their brand values, while also addressing challenges like ethics and content protection. The discussion highlighted the potential for "digital twins" and immersive collaboration in the workplace, with Gartner predicting widespread adoption.

feed.title: Microsoft announces four new employee workforce initiatives - Microsoft On the Issues
feed.summary: Microsoft is implementing four new workforce initiatives to enhance employee relationships and workplace culture. These changes include removing non-competition clauses for most U.S. employees, strengthening protections against disclosure of alleged misconduct, increasing pay transparency by publicly disclosing salary ranges, and conducting a civil rights audit of its workforce policies. These initiatives aim to empower employees, foster a safe environment for concerns, and reinforce the company's commitment to diversity and inclusion.

feed.title: Oracle closes $28B buy of ‘huge growth engine’ Cerner
feed.summary: Oracle has completed its $28.3 billion acquisition of electronic health record company Cerner, marking its largest acquisition to date and a significant move into the healthcare sector. The deal, an all-cash tender offer of $95 per share, aims to make Cerner an "anchor asset" for Oracle's expansion into healthcare, focusing on improved usability and voice-enabled interfaces for medical software. This acquisition is a substantial digital health deal, following other major acquisitions in the industry, and positions Cerner as a standalone business unit within Oracle.

feed.title: Procter & Gamble’s CIO believes passion is contagious. His latest passion: digitally remaking the 185-year-old company
feed.summary: Vittorio Cretella, CIO at Procter & Gamble, is leading a massive digital transformation of the 185-year-old company. P&G has partnered with Microsoft to leverage the Microsoft Cloud, aiming to accelerate its digital manufacturing platform and enrich the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). This collaboration seeks to improve productivity, speed up product delivery, boost customer satisfaction, and reduce costs, while also enhancing environmental sustainability through optimized energy and water consumption.

feed.title: A Full Return to the Office? Does ‘Never’ Work for You?
feed.summary: This article discusses the ongoing struggle between employers pushing for a return to office and employees who prefer remote work. It highlights that many companies are finding it difficult to enforce full-time office work, with some executives adapting to "remote-first" models or adopting hybrid approaches, while others, like C3 AI's CEO Tom Siebel, strongly advocate for employees to be in the office, citing competitive advantages and improved collaboration. The piece also notes a decrease in executive optimism regarding full in-office returns compared to early 2021.

feed.title: Playbook of the Week: Automate Your Response to Zero-Day Exploitation of Atlassian Confluence
feed.summary: This article introduces a Cortex XSOAR playbook designed to automate the response to the critical CVE-2022-26134 zero-day vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence Server and Data Center. The playbook helps security teams reduce manual effort by automating incident data enrichment, threat hunting across SIEMs and Palo Alto Networks environments, and remediation actions like blocking indicators and deploying detection rules. It is part of the Rapid Breach Response Pack, aiming to speed up the patching process and orchestration of security responses.

feed.title: HYCU funding to aid multi-cloud data protection, management
feed.summary: HYCU Inc. secured a $53 million Series B funding round, bringing its total funding to over $140 million. This investment will enable the company to expand its multi-cloud backup and recovery product line, increase its workforce, and develop a new data protection platform. HYCU aims to grow its customer base significantly and continues to pursue plans for an initial public offering, positioning itself as "recession-proof" in the data protection market.

feed.title: 10 jobs with the best future outlook for college grads—some pay more than $100,000 per year
feed.summary: The job market for 2022 college graduates is exceptionally strong, with nearly two job openings per unemployed person. ZipRecruiter identified 10 jobs with excellent future outlooks that require a bachelor's degree, based on Bureau of Labor Statistics projections. These roles, which include everything from elementary school teacher to financial manager, are expected to add tens to hundreds of thousands of new positions through 2030, with some paying over $100,000 annually.

feed.title: Dow dives 800 points, S&P 500 posts worst week since January after inflation hits 40-year high
feed.summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply on Friday, with the Dow dropping 880 points and the S&P 500 completing its worst week since January, following a higher-than-expected inflation report for May. The consumer price index reached its highest level since 1981, showing an 8.6% year-over-year increase, fueling concerns about a potential recession and prompting fears of a more aggressive Federal Reserve. Tech stocks, banks, and cyclical stocks were particularly impacted as the 2-year Treasury yield surged above 3%.

feed.title: P&G Levels Up Manufacturing With Machine Learning and AI
feed.summary: Procter & Gamble is partnering with Microsoft to implement AI, machine learning, and edge computing across over 100 manufacturing sites globally to improve productivity, reduce costs, and increase consumer satisfaction. This multiyear relationship will leverage Microsoft Azure to digitize and integrate data, enabling real-time, data-informed decisions and innovations in areas such as energy use, downtime reduction, and product quality. The collaboration includes the creation of a Digital Enablement Office to incubate and deploy high-priority business scenarios.

feed.title: 3 Excellent Dividend-Stock ETFs
feed.summary: This article highlights three excellent dividend-stock ETFs: Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG), Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD), and Vanguard International High Dividend Yield Index ETF (VYMI). These ETFs are lauded for their low cost, sensible index construction, and backing by investor-friendly firms, catering to different dividend investment strategies. The author provides details on each ETF's methodology, performance, and the types of companies it invests in.

feed.title: Hack Into Quantum Computing Boom With QQQ
feed.summary: Quantum computing, a disruptive technology with significant growth potential, is still in its early stages but offers various use cases. While some speculative companies exist, major players in this field are large-cap companies. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM) provide investors with exposure to quantum computing through their holdings in established tech giants like Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and Honeywell.

feed.title: Is the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) Right for You?
feed.summary: The Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) offers investors diversified exposure to companies benefiting from the metaverse's growth. This article examines METV's top holdings, including Meta Platforms, Nvidia, Roblox, Microsoft, and Autodesk, highlighting their roles in the metaverse ecosystem. It also discusses the fund's expense ratio and the potential market size of the metaverse industry.

feed.title: Google Agrees to Pay $118 Million to Settle Pay Discrimination Case (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Google has agreed to pay $118 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging systematic underpayment of women. The settlement covers approximately 15,500 women employed by Google in California since September 2013 and also mandates external oversight of its pay practices. Google denied wrongdoing, stating the settlement was in the best interest of all parties involved after five years of litigation.

feed.title: Google Engineer Claims AI System is Sentient; China's Tech Giants Flourish as Crackdown Eases
feed.summary: A Google engineer has been suspended after claiming that the company's LaMDA chatbot system shows signs of sentience, which Google denies, citing confidentiality breaches. Meanwhile, China's major tech companies like Baidu, Tencent, and Alibaba are experiencing a surge in share value as Beijing eases its regulatory crackdown on the sector. Twitter has also introduced a new "people-first" content moderation process to improve reporting of offensive content, especially amid Elon Musk's previous concerns about fake accounts.

feed.title: Oracle women stumble in pay bias suit while Google cuts a deal
authors: Malathi Nayak and Robert Burnson and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Women at Oracle Corp. face a setback in their pay disparity lawsuit as a judge tentatively revoked their class-action status, making it more difficult to proceed. Meanwhile, Google agreed to pay $118 million to settle a similar lawsuit alleging pay disparities for more than 15,000 female workers. The Google settlement includes provisions for independent oversight of hiring practices and pay equity studies.
